thread:
jordan: :rotating_light: multiple customers reporting truncated SSE streams from NA region since ~2026-03-15T08:30Z. Clients see partial output then reconnects; some get 401 on reconnect, others get duplicate chunks. Tickets: #4281 #4284. Repro steps attached. Please triage.

maria: ACK — oncall here, investigating. Which front-tier and model are affected? Any correlation to customer tier or route?

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-001. Pager duty notified. Link: https://redwood.status/inc/INC-20260315-001

alex: I’m looking at the runtime canary logs for na-west proxies. Seeing repeated "unexpected EOF while reading chunk" and backend 502s from the sse-proxy. Possible upstream abrt or token refresh race. Can someone drop request ids?

samir: From support tickets: customers using chat stream and also the raw completion SSE API. A few reported seeing the same partial tokens across reconnects — looks like clients resumed but server replayed last chunk.

ashley: Pulling proxy and LB metrics now. Hapoxy shows elevated queue times and a small spike in 5xx around 08:28-08:36Z. No host flaps. Kernel tcp_retransmits slightly up.

alex: paste of an error snippet from runtime logs:
```
2026-03-15T08:31:02.123Z [sse-proxy] request_id=rz-9f3a chunk_write_error: write tcp 10.0.1.12:443->10.2.3.4:59832: write: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T08:31:02.124Z [sse-proxy] request_id=rz-9f3a upstream_status=502
2026-03-15T08:31:03.001Z [auth] token_refresh request_id=rz-9f3a token_id=tr-77 err="expired token during reconnection"
```

maria: That token refresh line worries me — could be a race where client reconnects with a new token but server still in a half-closed streaming state causing dupes/truncation.

support-bot: Customer #4281 raw log (sanitized):
```
client: CONNECT /v1/stream?model=fast-chat
<event data: "partial: Hello wor">
socket closed by server
client reconnects -> 401
client refresh token -> reconnect -> receives "orld\n" (duplicate end)
```

samir: Also a billing note: two customers reported doubled token counts because client retried and server counted both attempts. Need to review dedupe on retries.

billing: Acknowledged. We can issue emergency credits while we investigate. Please list affected project ids and timestamps.

ashley: I’ve started a targeted rollback of the proxy keepalive tweak pushed last night to the na-west pool. Rolling back to previous config on 2/3 hosts now.

alex: Good call. The keepalive change shortened server-side write timeout which may have closed streams mid-chunk when clients did slow reconnects. Reverting should stop new events from being truncated.

jordan: For immediate mitigation: 1) enable non-streaming fallback for affected routes in Console (set sse_fallback=false->true) so clients auto-fallback to chunked polling, 2) add temporary rate-limit exemption for identity tokens that show reconnect spikes, 3) route heavy streams to eu-west as a regional failover.

ashley: Executed step 1 for route /v1/stream/chat: sse_fallback=true. Ops-bot will announce.

ops-bot: Rolling update: route /v1/stream/chat -> fallback enabled. Traffic will shift gradually. Monitor: https://redwood.console/routes/stream-chat

alex: Dev note — while we're rolling back, please avoid any further keepalive tweaks. I'll instrument additional logging around token refresh and connection-id mapping to validate the reconnection flow.

maria: Can someone paste a minimal repro we can send to customers and SREs? I'll coordinate on escalation email.

samir: Node repro we used in support (trimmed):
```
const http = require('http');
const req = http.request({ hostname: 'api.redwood.ai', path: '/v1/stream?model=fast-chat', headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <token>' } });
req.on('data', (chunk) => console.log('chunk', chunk.toString()));
req.on('end', () => console.log('end'));
req.end();
// Then force a reconnect mid-stream by rotating token and re-issuing request quickly
```

alex: Also tried curl streaming and saw "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n\n: chunked body..." then abrupt socket close with write: broken pipe. Adding a 500ms client-side keepalive prevents the truncation in our local repro — suggests timing window.

ashley: HAProxy config check: our tcp keepalive there was 45s; upstream runtime lowered it to 15s in canary. Revert completed on 2/3 and full rollback scheduled in 10m.

support-bot: Sent proactive notes to affected customers with temporary workarounds (enable polling fallback or increase client reconnect backoff). Templates used: support/templates/sse-truncation-2026-03-15.md

billing: Please DM me the customer IDs. We'll apply credits and confirm in ticket.

alex: Post-rollback, I'm not seeing the chunk_write_error in canary logs anymore. Latency and 5xx are trending down. Leaving instrumentation for 30m to ensure stability.

maria: Status update to #incidents at 09:15Z: rollback in progress, fallback enabled, regional failover prepared. No new escalations in last 12m. Will keep monitoring.

jordan: Final action items: 1) eng-runtime: add server-side dedupe for immediate-token-reconnects (alex), 2) eng-sre: add alert for token-refresh spikes correlated with chunk errors (ashley), 3) support: list affected customers and confirm credits applied (samir/billing), 4) product: update public status page once incident is mitigated. Timeline: review in 2 hours.

alex: I'll open a follow-up RFC for safer keepalive defaults and add unit tests for streaming reconnection semantics.

maria: Closing slack thread for now — moving to postmortem doc. If you have logs or unreconciled tickets, drop them in INC-20260315-001. Thanks everyone.
